Occurrences.Kwic: 唯士端坐不動。近臣報曰。聖駕在此。何不起。士曰。法地若動。一切不安。大士一日披衲．頂冠．靸履朝見。帝問。是僧邪。士以手指冠。帝曰。是道邪。士以手指靸履。帝曰。是俗邪。士以手指衲衣。大士心王銘曰。觀心空王。玄妙難測。無形無相。有大神力。能滅千災。成就萬德。體性雖空。能施法則。觀之無形。呼之有聲。為大法將。心戒傳經。水中鹽味。色裏膠青。決定是有。不見其形。心王亦爾。身內居停。

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Inscription on the Mind-King is a named verse attributed in Chan collections to Fu Dashi, beginning with contemplation of the empty mind-king.
EvidenceBody: Catalogues place it among transmitted Chan inscriptions, songs, and verses. Full texts begin by calling the mind-king formless yet effective and continue through compact paired lines.

A lamp biography records Baiyang Fashun awakening on hearing its line about salt in water and binder in color—present but not visibly separable—showing the titled work deployed inside a later awakening account.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A transmitted verse title becomes a quotable Chan source whose individual lines are raised as encounter evidence in biographies.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The entry identifies the work and its corpus deployment; it does not treat every occurrence of 'mind king' as a citation of the inscription.

ComparedThings: its attested grammatical and rhetorical deployments
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Catalogue and quotation uses all designate one titled verse work.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Mind-king, inscription, Fu Dashi, salt, water, color, and glue retrieve title and famous deployed line.

ModifierControls.Finding: Catalogue placement, title repetition, and full verse text establish a named inscription rather than a free phrase.

FamilyControls.Finding: A separate title attributed to Niutou Farong in some catalogues.
